Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When a repo has a dedicated money helper (e.g. ledgerly.money.round_money / to_money), route all monetary arithmetic and rounding through it rather than Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong totals.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: For weighted-average or division-based money results, remember to round the final quotient with the project's money-rounding helper; returning an unrounded Decimal division fails review even if tests pass.
## domain_facts
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: In ledgerly, ZERO is Decimal('0.00') and to_money() rejects float/bool inputs; use to_money() to normalize unit prices before multiplying by integer quantities, and return ZERO for empty/zero-quantity aggregates.

item.content: When validating integer inputs, explicitly reject bool (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since bool is a subclass of int and True/False would otherwise pass as quantities.
Don't forget state guards: mutating operations like add_line must check invoice.status == 'draft' and raise the project's BillingError('invalid_state', ...) before doing any work.
In ledgerly, BillingError(code, detail) is the standard error type; existing codes include 'invalid_state', 'invalid_quantity', and 'negative_amount' — reuse these codes for consistency.
